title: Water Act and Murray-Darling Basin Plan
summary: From 3 March 2008 the Water Act 2007 set up Basin-wide management of the Murray-Darling, including the Murray-Darling Basin Authority, the Basin Plan (made in 2012) and rules for water markets. Irrigators can buy and sell water, but report to both state and Commonwealth agencies.

instruments.title: Basin Plan 2012
instruments.provisions: sustainable diversion limits and water trading rules

commenced.what: Sections 3 to 256 and Schedules 1 to 4 commenced

direction_rationale: Water markets let water move to its most valuable uses; farmers told the Productivity Commission that being able to trade water had significantly boosted their productivity, while also reporting the same data to state and Commonwealth agencies.

verified.notes: Assent from the Federal Register; commencement on 3 March 2008 from section 2 (a proclaimed day, or six months after assent at the latest). Basin Plan making date from the Federal Register.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Basin-wide water markets let water move to higher-value uses, which farmers say has lifted their productivity. The cost is a second layer of reporting to Commonwealth agencies on top of state licensing.

marks.reason: Tradeable water lets prices guide water to its most valuable uses.
Irrigators and water operators report similar data to state and Commonwealth agencies.

history.what: The Basin Plan 2012 was made under the Act, setting sustainable diversion limits and water trading rules.
